 ATP Brussels Day 2 Predictions Including Jacob Fearnley vs Hugo Gaston 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 First-round action at the ATP European Open in Brussels continues with home favorite Raphael Collignon set to return after an injury absence. Seven matches are scheduled on Day 2, which also includes Jacob Fearnley’s meeting against Hugo Gaston. Who will reach the second round?
 ATP Brussels Day 2 Predictions
 Nishesh Basavareddy vs Raphael Collignon
 Head-to-head: Basavareddy 1-0 Collignon
 Nishesh Basavareddy had an exceptional week in qualifying. He did not drop his serve in two matches. Raphael Collignon returns to Brussels as an improved player. Last year, Collignon produced a tremendous run (semifinalist) thanks to wins over Zizou Bergs and Alejandro Davidovich Fokina. It will be tough to replicate that run. Playing on home soil adds even more pressure. Moreover, Collignon has been out of form since reaching the Gstaad final and was nursing a knee injury before this tournament.
 Prediction: Basavareddy in 2 
 Mariano Navone vs Juan Manuel Cerundolo
 Head-to-head: Navone 4-2 Cerundolo
 All six meetings between Mariano Navone and Juan Manuel Cerundolo were contested on clay courts. That said, both players have shown improved form on hard courts in recent months. But it is Navone who has produced stellar results on the surface, including an eye-catching five-set win over Novak Djokovic at the US Open.
 Prediction: Navone in 3 
 Jan 13, 2025; Melbourne, Victoria, Australia; Mariano Navone of Argentina hits a forehand during his match against Jack Draper of United Kingdom in the first round of the men’s singles at the 2025 Australian Open at Melbourne Park. Mandatory Credit: Mike Frey-Imagn Images 
 Jacob Fearnley vs Hugo Gaston
 Head-to-head: first meeting
 Despite going into the Olbia Challenger final as the heavy favorite, Jacob Fearnley fell to a shock straight-sets defeat to Damir Dzumhur last weekend. With just a day of rest, Fearnley faces a possible first-round exit in Brussels. Hugo Gaston thrives in these conditions where his forehand creates tricky crosscourt patterns. If Fearnley is a step slow after a long week in Olbia, Gaston should make him pay.
 Prediction: Gaston in 3
